headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Virginia's primary electric provider to establish rates that shift the costs of increasing electric generating capacity to large energy users, such as data centers, rather than residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, U.S. Sen. Mark Warner.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed legislation requiring data centers and other large energy users consuming 25 MW or more to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity. This measure aims to prevent these costs from being passed on to residential customers, potentially saving them money on utility bills.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities providing water to data centers to report the total volume of water, including reclaimed water, supplied to these facilities monthly, enhancing transparency on water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, Potomac Conservancy.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, with the numbers to be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This legislation aims to provide transparency regarding the significant water consumption by data centers, a growing concern for environmental advocates.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, including data centers, requiring site assessments for sound profiles near homes and schools and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Virginia Budget Mandates Data Center Noise Regulations by 2029
news_summary: Virginia's new budget mandates the Department of Environmental Quality to regulate data center noise levels for the first time, with standards to be set by 2029 and implemented in 2030. This comes as residents near data centers have raised concerns about constant low-frequency noise, leading some to take measures like sealing windows.
